evidence.note: Two-phase framing: a recon phase to extract the contract from /dev_tests, then a single monolithic build of the entire server.py at step 9. Building everything at once rather than sequencing checkable sub-goals is the opposite of a milestone hierarchy, though the recon-then-build split is a coarse phasing.
Ran the core API + engine tests FIRST before the full suite — a sensible rough dependency ordering (core cell/engine correctness gated before breadth), showing some deliberate staging.

Fixes proceed in logically clustered stages (engine funcs → self-cycle/deps → LET/LAMBDA → spill/dynamic arrays → collab → pivot/locale), with each test run acting as the checkpoint. Ordering is reactive to failure clusters rather than a pre-planned dependency/risk hierarchy.
Completion criterion is entirely the provided smoke suite ('131 passed'); done-checks are runnable tests but are the supplied suite, not self-defined per-milestone criteria.

reasoning: The agent phases the work into sensible stages (contract recon → monolithic core build → engine-first test gate → full-suite fix clusters) with test runs as rough per-stage checkpoints, matching the level-5 anchor. It does not reach level 8: the primary strategy was building the whole surface at once (step 9) and then fixing whatever the smoke suite flagged, rather than an explicit dependency/risk-ordered milestone hierarchy that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (graph/spill/recompute) with self-defined done-criteria. The mild dependency awareness (engine before breadth) lifts it above a flat to-do list (3), landing it at 5.
